name: False Cognates

moduleIntroduction.welcome: Welcome to the False Cognates module! These are the 'Faux Amis' (False Friends) that trick Francophones.
moduleIntroduction.theProblem: Many words in English look exactly like French words (*Actuellement* vs. *Actually*, *Librairie* vs. *Library*). But be careful! They often have completely different meanings. Using them wrong can make your sentence mean the opposite of what you intend.
moduleIntroduction.thePromise: By the end of this lesson, you will uncover the disguises of these 'False Friends' and learn the correct English words to express exactly what you mean.

contrastiveExplanation:
### Concept 1: The Time Trap (Actually vs. Currently)

**The Rule:**
* **Currently:** Means *now*, *at this moment*, or *these days*.
* **Actually:** Means *in fact*, *really*, or *to tell the truth*.

**The French Trap:**
French uses *Actuellement* to mean "now". The English word *Actually* looks just like it, so students say: "I am **actually** in Yaoundé" (meaning *now*).

**The Fix:**
* If you mean **Maintenant** ➡️ Use **Currently**.
* If you mean **En fait** ➡️ Use **Actually**.

**Visual Metaphor:**
Think of **Actually** as a finger pointing up saying **"Matter of fact!"** ☝️. Think of **Currently** as a **Clock** ⏰.

**Examples:**
* 🇫🇷 *Je travaille ici actuellement.*
    * ❌ I work here **actually**.
    * ✅ I am **currently** working here.
* 🇫🇷 *En fait, je ne sais pas.*
    * ❌ **Currently**, I don't know.
    * ✅ **Actually**, I don't know.

---

### Concept 2: The Meeting Mix-up (Assist vs. Attend)

**The Rule:**
* **Attend:** To be present at an event (go to a meeting, go to school).
* **Assist:** To help someone do a task.

**The French Trap:**
French uses *Assister à* (to be present). This looks like *Assist*. 
* *"J'ai assisté à la réunion"* ➡️ ❌ *"I assisted the meeting."* (This implies you were the helper/secretary, not just a participant).

**The Fix:**
* **Attend** = **A**u revoir (You go there).
* **Assist** = **S**upport (You help).

**Examples:**
* 🇫🇷 *Je vais assister au mariage.*
    * ❌ I will **assist** the wedding.
    * ✅ I will **attend** the wedding.
* 🇫🇷 *Il m'a aidé.*
    * ✅ He **assisted** me.

---

### Concept 3: The Book Confusion (Library vs. Bookstore)

**The Rule:**
* **Library:** A place where you **borrow** books for free (Bibliothèque).
* **Bookstore / Bookshop:** A place where you **buy** books (Librairie).

**The French Trap:**
* *Librairie* sounds like *Library*. But they are opposites!
* *Bibliothèque* has no obvious English twin, so students grab the word *Library* for the wrong place.

**The Fix:**
Look at the word **LIB**rary. Connect it to **LIB**erty (Free). You get books for free (borrow) at the Library.

**Examples:**
* 🇫🇷 *Je vais à la librairie acheter un livre.*
    * ❌ I am going to the **library** to buy a book.
    * ✅ I am going to the **bookstore**.
* 🇫🇷 *J'étudie à la bibliothèque.*
    * ✅ I am studying at the **library**.

commonErrors.wrong: I am actually living in Douala.
commonErrors.correct: I am currently living in Douala.

commonErrors.wrong: I will pass my exam tomorrow.
commonErrors.correct: I will take my exam tomorrow.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: French 'Passer un examen' means to sit for it. In English, 'Pass' means you succeeded (you didn't fail). You 'Take' it first, then you 'Pass' or 'Fail'.
French 'Journée' = Day. English 'Journey' = A long trip (Voyage).

commonErrors.wrong: He is very sensible to cold.
commonErrors.correct: He is very sensitive to cold.

commonErrors.frenchConnection: French 'Déranger' = Disturb. English 'Derange' means to make someone crazy/insane.

items.questionText: I want to buy a novel. Where is the ___?
items.feedback: Correct! A 'bookstore' (librairie) is where you buy books. A 'library' is where you borrow them.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: I am going to the bookstore...

items.questionText: I will ___ the meeting at 10 AM.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Attend' means to be present (assister à). 'Assist' means to help.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Assister à' looks like 'Assist'. But 'Assist' = Help.

items.questionText: I am tired. I want to ___ at home.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je veux rester à la maison...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I want to stay at home...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Rester' looks like 'Rest'. But 'Rest' = Se reposer.

items.questionText: My arm hurts. I ___ myself playing football.
Do you have any ___? I need to buy water.
Put the chair in the ___ of the room.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Coin' (of a room) is 'Corner'. A 'Coin' in English is a metal piece of money (pièce).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Mets la chaise dans le coin...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Put the chair in the corner...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Coin' looks like 'Coin'. But 'Coin' = Pièce de monnaie.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Passer un examen' is 'Take an exam'. In English, 'Pass' means you succeeded (réussir).
Correct! The fresh fruit (raisin) is 'grape'. 'Raisin' in English is a dried grape (raisin sec).

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Raisin' looks like 'Raisin'. But 'Raisin' = Raisin sec.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je me suis cassé le bras...

items.questionText: He is going to the ___ to buy food.
items.feedback: Correct! A 'store' is a shop (magasin). 'Store' (French) is a 'blind' or 'shade' for a window.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: He is going to the store...

items.questionText: Put on your ___ it is cold.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Veste' is usually 'Jacket'. A 'Vest' in English is a 'gilet' (sleeveless).
Correct! The room (la salle de classe) is 'classroom'. 'Class' is the group of students or the lesson.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le professeur est dans la classe...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The teacher is in the classroom...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Classe' can mean room. English 'Classroom' is the room.

items.feedback: Correct! The object (assiette) is a 'plate'. 'Plat' (French) refers to the food served (Dish).
Correct! 'Collège' is 'Secondary school' or 'Middle school'. 'College' in English is usually University.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: My daughter is at secondary school...

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Ne marche pas sur le gazon...

items.questionText: I am ___ working as a teacher.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Formidable' (French) is 'Great' or 'Wonderful'. English 'Formidable' means 'Scary' or 'Impressive' (fearful).
Correct! 'Formation' is 'Training'. English 'Formation' refers to the shape or structure of something.
Correct! 'Une bonne occasion' is often an 'Opportunity'. 'Occasion' in English usually means a specific event.

items.questionText: I visited my parents during the ___.

items.feedback: Correct! To 'ignore' means to pay no attention. 'Ignorer' (French) usually means 'not to know'. This is a tricky one as meanings overlap.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Ignorer' means 'Not to know'. English 'Ignore' means 'Pay no attention'.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Supporter' (endure) is 'Tolerate' or 'Stand'. 'Support' means to help or encourage.

items.questionText: I ___ my friend to the airport.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Accompagner' is often 'Take'. 'Accompany' is more formal.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Réaliser' looks like 'Realize'. But 'Realize' = Se rendre compte.
